# More SoundObject types

Add these from a SoundObject layer's **Add SoundObject** menu, select the
object, and open **Score Object Editor** to edit its type-specific contents.
The [SoundObjects overview](soundobjects.qmd) explains placement, shared
properties, Note Processors, and Time Behavior. A **Test** button in an
object editor previews generated score text; it does not audition audio.

## Text and generated notes

**Comment** stores notes for the composer and emits no Csound score
events. Use it to label a section without adding sound.

**JavaScriptObject** runs its script in Blue's JavaScript session to
produce score text. Its generated notes then pass through the object's
Note Processors and Time Behavior. **PythonObject** and
**ClojureObject** similarly generate notes through the Java runtime's
Jython and Clojure sessions. Their synchronous generation path cannot
run without that service; check runtime status and use the editor's Test
action before a full render. A project's **Clojure** properties tab can
name dependencies for Clojure content. These languages are distinct
from a JavaScript *Instrument*, whose orchestra generation has a
[current limitation](instruments.qmd#javascript-instrument).

**External** sends the editor's code text to a configured external
command and parses the returned score. Enter a **Command Line** in the
object editor, then use **Test** to see what it produces. The command
must be available on the computer doing the render; copied `.blue`
projects do not supply the executable. Treat the command output as
score text and check file paths before sharing the project.

**ObjectBuilder** combines a small widget interface with code that
generates score. Its language selector supports JavaScript, Python,
Clojure, and an external command. Python and Clojure need the Java
runtime; External needs its command executor. The interface supplies
widget values to the code. Test the object after changing its language,
command, or widget names.

## Pattern generators

**JMask** generates notes from parameter generators and modifiers. In
its editor, choose which parameters are visible, configure their
generators, and press **Test** to inspect the resulting score. Enable
**Seed** and set a value when you need repeatable random output. An
unseeded pattern may change on each generation.

### TrackerObject

**TrackerObject** is a step grid with multiple tracks. Use **+ TRACK**,
set **STEPS** and **Steps per beat**, then edit each track's instrument,
note template, and columns to match its Csound `p` fields. **USE KEYBOARD
NOTES** and **OCTAVE** aid pitch entry. **TEST** previews generated
score, and the **Keyboard Shortcuts** button shows the current grid
commands. The old Java shortcut table is not a reliable Blue 3 key map.

## Lines and self-contained sounds

**LineObject** draws one or more control lines. Add a line in the
definitions pane, give it a variable name and range, then edit points
in the canvas. The current canvas hints that **Alt-click** adds a point;
its right-click menu offers further actions. Blue generates supporting
tables and instruments for the line when rendering.

**ZakLineObject** uses a similar line editor but writes to Zak channels.
Set each line's **Zak Channel** and the object's **Zak Space** before
generating. Check that these channel numbers agree with the Csound
code that reads them.

**Sound** contains its own BlueSynthBuilder and produces an instrument
and a note for that one object. Edit its interface and code in the
Sound editor. Use its local automation controls for values that vary
over the object's duration. For an instrument reused by many Score
objects, put it in the [Orchestra](orchestra.qmd) instead.

## Historical Cecilia module

The Blue 2 **CeciliaModule** entry describes an unfinished Java Blue
SoundObject. Blue 3 does not register a CeciliaModule type or offer it
in the Add SoundObject menu. The original text remains in the
[Blue 2 source edition](https://github.com/kunstmusik/blue-manual/tree/7a92066a2aa8f0370026ba9527c158643c2935a1); it is not an instruction for
the current application.
